finding.title: Strip row.entityKey out of the outbox dead-letter analytics event (leaks profileId + sefariaRef)
finding.why: For OutboxEntityKind.completion rows the outbox entityKey is literally `${profileId}:${sefariaRef}:${stageId}:${trackType}:${curriculumId}` (completion_writer.dart:747). When a row hits _maxAttempts, both dead-letter sites fire `_analytics.logEvent(LogEvents.sync.outboxDeadLettered, parameters: {..., 'entity_key': row.entityKey, ...})`, sending that exact string — a per-child profile ID plus the specific Torah reference the child studied — to Firebase Analytics. This is a NEW instance of the two categories PV-1 explicitly names as banned (`sefaria_ref`, `profile_id`), distinct from the already-baselined analytics_service.dart:56/82/87 gap, and it fires automatically (no user action) for a children's app subject to COPPA/GDPR-K whenever a sync failure persists through 10 retries — plausible on any prolonged connectivity or rules issue.
finding.recommendation: Never pass row.entityKey (or any of its `:`-joined constituents) as a logEvent parameter. Emit only structurally opaque fields (`entity_kind`, `attempts`); if a stable debug identifier is needed, hash entityKey locally before logging it, never send it raw.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test asserts the dead-letter logEvent() parameters map never contains an 'entity_key' (or any key whose value embeds sefariaRef/profileId) for a completion row.
Extend the PV-1 audit grep (or a custom_lint rule) to fail when row.entityKey / a raw outbox entityKey flows into any logEvent(...parameters...) call.
